content.title: About
content.content: Chicken nuggets are small pieces of chicken breast that are breaded and deep‑fried or baked. They are a popular quick snack and are commonly served in fast‑food restaurants, casual eateries, and at home.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial nugget recipe was created in the 1970s by McDonald’s.
Traditional breading uses a mix of flour, breadcrumbs and spices, but there are versions with cornflakes or nut crumbs.
Nuggets are often served with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, sweet chili, cheese and others.
In some countries they are called “chicken bites” or “chicken sticks.”
Vegetarian nuggets made from soy protein mimic the taste and texture of chicken.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Nuggets contain niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: When prepared with a light coating, nuggets can fit into low‑carb diets.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Traditional deep‑fried nuggets are rich in saturated fat and calories, which may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt in the breading and sauces increases sodium intake, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Breadings often contain gluten, dairy or egg, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Cooking at high temperatures can create trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Undercooked pieces may harbor harmful bacteria; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve nuggets hot, usually with dipping sauces. They can be added to salads, wraps, or used in dishes like nugget‑burgers. For a healthier option, bake at 200 °C for 15‑20 minutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked nuggets in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Frozen nuggets last up to 2 months; reheat thoroughly before eating.
